title: telemetry-driven kernel hinting for MIG-aware prefill scheduling
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Reduce appliable tail latency and per-token compute cost for prefill-heavy workloads on heterogeneous GPU farms (H100 / L40S / A10) by surfacing lightweight runtime telemetry and using it to drive a kernel-hinting layer that biases kernel selection and prefill/decode scheduling decisions per-MIG partition and per-request shape.
background: We've observed that prefill (encoder-like long-sequence) and decode (autoregressive) phases have different ideal kernel paths depending on token density, sequence-length distribution, KV cache hit-rate, and MIG partition geometry. Static kernel selection heuristics mispredict on mixed tenant workloads and suboptimal clock states (boost/eco) cause inconsistent throughput. Existing efforts (kernel-packetizer, clock steering) reduced variance but still rely mainly on global heuristics. This ticket prototypes a telemetry -> kernel-hint pipeline to provide per-request hints (preferred kernel family, warp/occupancy target, clock preference) and uses those hints in the prefill scheduler to improve packing and reduce kernel warm-up overhead.
acceptance_criteria: - Implement a low-overhead telemetry producer that emits per-request features (seq_len, batch_pos, avg_token_density, estimated_kv_size, tenant_mig_size) and aggregate per-worker histograms.
acceptance_criteria_2: - Add a kernel-hint consumer in the scheduler that maps telemetry to kernel-family hints without blocking the hot-path (<= 10us added p50 per request).
acceptance_criteria_3: - End-to-end experiment on a mixed-tenancy H100 cluster: p99 prefill latency reduced by >= 12% and average token cost reduced by >= 8% compared to baseline for the target workload mix.
technical_design: 1) Telemetry schema: fixed small vector of strings/ints emitted at prefill start (seq_len_bucket, avg_token_density_bucket, estimated_kv_mb, mig_partition_slots, recent_batch_variance). Keep payload < 128 bytes.
technical_design_2: 2) Hinting model: start with rule-based mapping optimized from offline microbenchmarks (per-GPU-family). Later iterate to a small decision tree model for noisy boundaries. Hints: {kernel_family: {fmha_fast, fmha_stable, gemm_large, gemm_small}, clock_mode: {boost, balanced}, prefill_slot_target: integer}.
technical_design_3: 3) Scheduler integration: Use hints to pick prefill packing buckets and kernel candidates. When multiple tenants share a MIG slice, prefer kernels with lower transient memory working set. If hint and current worker kernel disagree, allow asynchronous kernel prewarming to avoid blocking decode.
tradeoffs: - Rule-based mapping is predictable and debuggable but may underfit complex interactions; small learned model improves hit-rate but needs training data and validation across HW families.
tradeoffs_2: - Emitting telemetry adds overhead and cardinality to logs; must ensure telemetry path is sampled or aggregated to avoid cost blowup.
implementation_steps: 1) Define telemetry schema and add lightweight emitter in runtime request entrypoint (prefill start).
2) Add per-worker telemetry aggregator and periodic histogram flush to in-memory ring buffer.
3) Implement rule-based hint mapper using microbenchmark results per-device and per-MIG configuration.
4) Expose kernel-hint API in scheduler and implement prewarm path for hinted kernels.
5) Add feature flag and runtime config (telemetry_sampling_ratio, hinting_enabled).
6) Run offline microbenchmarks across H100/L40S/A10 and generate mapping tables.
7) Run canary against 10% of traffic, measure p50/p99 and token cost.
8) Iterate on mapping, add small decision-tree model if needed, and expand rollout.
test_plan: Unit tests for telemetry emitter and mapper. Integration tests that simulate mixed sequence-length batches and validate chosen kernel families. Microbench harness that runs prioritized benchmark matrix for H100/L40S/A10 across MIG partition sizes (1g/2g/3g) measuring latency and SM occupancy. Canary A/B with metric collection and automatic rollback if p99 regresses >5%.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag behind config: telemetry_sampling_ratio=0.001 for initial alpha, hinting_enabled=false.
rollout_plan_2: 2) Internal perf experiments in dedicated cluster with synthetic workload (prefill-heavy + bursty decode).
rollout_plan_3: 3) Canary on 10% of production traffic in a single region and single GPU family (H100). Collect metrics 48h. If stable, expand to L40S and A10 in additional 25% traffic windows.
observability_and_alerting: Dashboards: kernel_hint_accept_rate, hinted_vs_fallback_latency, telemetry_emit_errors, per-mig_kernel_choice_distribution. Alert on sudden increase in kernel_fallback_rate or telemetry_emit_overhead > 50us p95.
risks_mitigation: Risk: mis-hinting causes tail regressions. Mitigation: conservative mapping, short-circuit fallback to baseline kernel if p99 degrades; feature flag quick-toggle. Risk: telemetry cardinality -> sample aggressively and aggregate on-worker.
dependencies_detail: Requires updated microbenchmark matrix from infra (ENG-26114) and improved prefill profiling hooks (ENG-35892) to get reliable kv_size estimates.
